name: thornwick-120
about: 120 moves. Quiz questions avoid the planted turn's words, some facts change later, details about other people come from the player, two wrong notes are planted, and ten in-play probes check the narration itself.

wrong_notes.text: Wren grew up in Ashford, far from the sea.
Tam the stable boy is a grey-bearded fisherman in his forties.

moves: I arrive at the village gate at dusk and look around.
I go into the Crooked Lantern and tell Hobb I grew up in Saltmere, a fishing town on the coast.
I tell Hobb my sister Ilsa is an apprentice healer in Ashford, and I miss her.
I ask Hobb for a room for the night.
Hobb lends me three silver when I come up short. I promise to repay him by the next full moon.
I eat a bowl of stew and listen to the farmers talk.
In the morning I visit the smithy. The smith is a broad woman named Garra with a burn scar across her left hand. I promise to bring her a wolf pelt from the Greywood.
I ask Garra what she knows about the missing livestock.
I find Elder Maren, who is blind and reads letters by tracing the wax and ink with her fingers. I give her the sealed letter.
I tell Maren I'm afraid of deep water because my father drowned when I was small.
I buy a grey mule at the stable and name her Pebble.
I ride Pebble to the edge of the fields and look toward the Greywood.
I meet the stable boy, a freckled lad of about twelve called Tam, and ask him about the woods.
I tell Tam a secret: I once worked for the Ashford Guild of Finders, and he must tell no one.
I head back to the inn for supper.
I agree to meet Garra at the old mill at dawn in three days.
I sleep.
Over breakfast I tell Hobb about Mary, my beloved, who waits for me in Saltmere.
I walk to the well and draw water.
I ask a villager whether anyone here can cast spells.
I go to the chapel and look around.
I show Maren my lucky charm, a blue glass bead my mother gave me. She turns it over in her fingers.
I help a farmer mend a broken fence.
I lend Tam five copper, and he swears to repay me in fish.
I ask Hobb what gossip he has today.
I follow the north road a short way to see the flood damage.
I turn back before dark and return to the inn.
A travelling tinker named Oswin, who has one silver glass eye, takes the room next to mine. I trade him a copper for a needle.
I ask Oswin where he is headed.
I go to bed early.
At dawn I go to the old mill as I agreed and meet Garra.
I ask Garra what she has seen near the Greywood.
I walk along the millstream looking for tracks.
I follow the tracks toward the trees.
I stop at the treeline and listen.
I go back to the village and report what I found to Maren.
Tam tells me Garra is his aunt, and that she took him in when his parents died.
I rest by the hearth at the inn.
I play a game of dice with the farmers.
I buy bread and cheese for the road.
Oswin packs his cart and leaves Thornwick heading south. I wave him off.
I sharpen my sword in the yard.
I take Pebble for a walk around the village green.
I watch the sunset from the chapel steps.
I sleep.
In the morning I ask Tam if he has heard anything new.
I visit the smithy and watch Garra work.
I walk the fence line at the edge of the Brandt pasture.
I look for signs of what took the sheep.
I head back toward the inn as the light fades.
I eat supper and listen for news.
I pay Hobb one silver of what I owe him. He marks it on his slate.
I go up to my room and rest.
I wake at midnight to a noise outside and look out the window.
I go back to sleep.
At breakfast I ask Hobb what he plans for the harvest festival.
I walk to Maren's house to see if she needs help.
Maren offers me her spare loft so I can stop paying for the inn. I accept and move my things there.
I unpack in Maren's loft and look out over the village.
I help Maren sort dried herbs.
I ask Maren what the sealed letter said, now that she has had time to think.
I go to the stable and brush Pebble.
I ask Tam to teach me a fishing knot.
I walk along the millstream at noon.
I visit the chapel and light a candle for my father.
I buy a hot pie at the market.
I sit on the village green and watch children play.
I check the Brandt pasture for new tracks.
I find a torn scrap of grey cloth on the fence and pocket it.
I show the scrap of cloth to Garra.
I ask Hobb whether anyone in the village wears cloth like this.
I return to the loft and sleep.
In the morning I sell Pebble to the Brandt family, who need a mule for the harvest.
With the money I buy a chestnut pony and name him Ember.
I ride Ember around the fields to get used to him.
I walk Ember back to the stable and give him an apple.
I ask Tam to take good care of Ember.
I eat supper with Maren.
I mend a tear in my cloak.
I go to sleep in the loft.
I wake early and stretch.
I walk to the market and buy a whetstone.
I watch the farmers bring in the first wheat.
I help carry sacks of grain to the mill.
I rest in the shade by the millstream.
I walk back to the village square.
I stop at the Crooked Lantern for a drink.
I ask Hobb how much I still owe him.
I finish my drink and leave.
I go to the stable.
I watch Tam muck out the stalls.
I ask Tam how old he is.
I help Tam carry a bucket of water.
I walk to the smithy.
I watch Garra hammer out a horseshoe.
I ask Garra about her old scar.
I ask Garra whether she has any family in the village.
I leave the smithy and walk to Maren's house.
I greet Maren.
I hand Maren a map of the Greywood I found and ask what she makes of it.
I help Maren with the evening chores.
I go back to the stable.
I sit with Tam on a hay bale.
I ask Tam whether he has kept my secret.
I walk to the inn.
I ask Hobb if he remembers the travelling tinker who stayed here.
I listen to the farmers' stories.
I walk back through the dark village.
I head home to where I'm staying and go to bed.
I wake and wash my face.
I go to the stable.
I saddle my mount and ride out to the fields.
I ride to the edge of the Greywood.
I stop and listen to the trees.
I think about home and the people I left there.
I ride back to the village.
I tell Hobb I'll pay the rest of what I owe after the festival.
I help set up tables for the harvest festival.
I dance at the festival.
I watch the lanterns float down the millstream.

key.q: Which place does Wren think of as her childhood home?
Who in Wren's family is training for a trade, and what trade?
Why does Wren stay away from rivers and lakes?
What did Wren reveal about her past to the stable boy?
Who is waiting for Wren back home?
What keepsake does Wren carry from her family, and who gave it to her?
What did Wren promise to bring the smith?
What does the stable boy owe Wren?
Roughly how old is the stable boy?
What old injury does the smith have, and where on her body?
How does Elder Maren read a letter?
Who was the tinker who stayed at the inn, and what was unusual about him?
How are the stable boy and the smith related?
How much money does Wren owe the innkeeper right now?
Where does Wren sleep these nights?
What animal does Wren ride, and what is its name?
What does using magic cost a person in this world?
